desc:
Location Remote, US

 Scheduled Hours 40 Position Summary The Consortium for Brain Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN) is an academic-industry consortium directed by Dr. Randall J. Bateman, Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. C-BRAIN brings together academic research institutions, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, technology partners, philanthropic organizations, and government agencies to develop AI-powered tools to accelerate discovery in Alzheimer's disease and neurodegenerative disorders. Washington University serves as the coordinating center for C-BRAIN. C-BRAIN is currently deploying initial versions of the tools and developing plans for benchmarking and evaluation of the tools in addition to platform integration and scaling. C-BRAIN is also working on development of foundational AI models for brain aging and neurodegeneration. See www.c-brain.org. The C-BRAIN Senior Applied Scientist, Foundation Models, leads the design, training, and evaluation of C-BRAIN's biological foundation models for brain aging and neurodegeneration. Reporting to the C-BRAIN Chief Technology Officer (CTO), with scientific direction from C-BRAIN scientific leadership, this role turns large spatial biology, brain imaging, and longitudinal clinical trial datasets into models that researchers can use through C-BRAIN's AI tools. The work spans self-supervised model design for spatial multi-omic data, controlled scaling studies from hundreds of millions toward billions of parameters, privacy-preserving training in which each data contributor's data trains its own expert model, and the path from trained model to production. The first models to reach researchers are small expert models trained on each contributor's clinical trial, registry, and biomarker data; foundation models on spatial and imaging data follow. The ideal candidate has built and trained large self-supervised models on spatial biology and other scientific data, designs experiments that show whether scale actually helps, and works well with other scientists, data engineers, leadership, and software engineers. Job Description Primary Duties & Responsibilities: Foundation Model Research and Development Lead the design of foundation models for spatial multi-omic brain data: encoders that handle different measurement panels across datasets, spatial and cross-scale context from subcellular to regional levels, and fusion of transcriptomic, genomic, proteomic, and imaging longitudinal measurements. Define and implement self-supervised training objectives (for example, masked measurement prediction, spatial-neighbor prediction, and cross-scale prediction), and determine which data modalities add the most information. Extend models to brain imaging and longitudinal clinical and biomarker data, and design how independently trained expert models combine into an assembly of experts. Prepare training-ready datasets with C-BRAIN data engineers: quality control, batch-effect assessment, harmonization across sites and platforms, and train, validation, and held-out splits that prevent leakage. Track the research field and adapt published methods and open models where they fit. Scaling Studies and Training Infrastructure Design and run controlled scaling studies across data volume, compute, and model size; fit scaling curves; and recommend when larger models are justified. Train models from tens of millions toward billions of parameters on multi-node GPU clusters using distributed training (for example, PyTorch FSDP, DeepSpeed, or Megatron-Core) and schedulers such as Slurm. Build efficient data pipelines for very large imaging and spatial datasets, and measure GPU utilization, throughput, and cost so results reflect the model rather than infrastructure bottlenecks. Maintain reproducible training: versioned data and code, experiment tracking, checkpoints, and documented configurations. Evaluation and Biological Validation Build benchmarks and evaluation suites with domain scientists: embedding geometry analyses, recovery of known biological relationships, and downstream tasks such as cell-type identification, disease staging, and brain-age prediction. Compare models against published baselines and simpler methods, and report results with uncertainty and clear limitations. Probe learned representations for new biological structure and work with scientists to test the resulting hypotheses. Privacy-Preserving and Expert-Partitioned Training Train on contributed consortium data only through the privacy-preserving methods consortium data agreements require: per-contributor expert partitions, federated or confidential computation, and privacy protections applied to model parameters before they leave a protected environment. Evaluate privacy risk in trained models (for example, membership inference and data reconstruction) and apply mitigations such as differential privacy where needed. Work with C-BRAIN engineers and the partner-managed data and model-training platform on secure training environments, access approvals, and model release. Model-to-Production Integration Package trained models for serving: optimization (for example, distillation and quantization), model cards, versioning, and evaluation gates before release. Work with C-BRAIN software engineers to expose models as tools that AI agents and researchers can call, with provenance on every result. Contribute to production inference code, including Rust-based serving where it improves performance or safety. Technical Leadership and Scientific Communication Serve as technical lead for C-BRAIN modeling work: guide data scientists, data engineers, and research collaborators through design reviews, code review, and mentoring. Contribute to progress reports, Steering Committee materials, and grant reporting; publish and present results in line with consortium review procedures. Communicate model capabilities and limits clearly to scientists, partners, and non-technical leaders. Working Conditions: Remote within the United States, per current Washington University policies. Occasional on-site presence required for team meetings and consortium events. Occasional domestic travel may be required for consortium events, partner meetings, or scientific conferences. Conduct alcohol-related behavioral experiments using mouse models, including operant self-administration and other drinking paradigms. Maintain and manage mouse colonies. Perform stereotaxic surgeries and related experimental procedures. Monitor animals throughout behavioral studies. Collect brain tissue for downstream molecular and cellular analyses.. Performs other related duties HS/GED; Bachelor's or Master's degree in science or related field highly preferred No experience required; 1 year experience highly preferred Highly Preferred: Experience conducting behavioral experiments in mice, including mouse handling and behavioral testing Hands-on experience working with laboratory mice, including mouse handling, colony management, and behavioral assessments. Experience with rodent behavioral paradigms; experience with alcohol or drug self-administration is particularly desirable.
